A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SeTok/SeTokIM research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison, including matching relocated analyses and renumbered displays.

before.justification: v3 reports original reconstruction, visual understanding, generation, editing, and segmentation results, together with component and tokenizer ablations.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and adds language-retention experiments, an additional loss ablation, and a comparison using the same training dataset as LLaVA-1.5.

M1.justification: The dynamic clustering algorithm, token merger, reconstruction and contrastive objectives, autoregressive modeling, and mask decoder remain unchanged. Appendix D.1 expands the detokenizer description without establishing a revised procedure; the additional loss variants are experimental ablations.

E1.justification: v4 adds language-only knowledge evaluation on MMLU across humanities, STEM, social sciences, and other subjects, substantially broadening evaluation beyond the existing vision-language tasks. Table 14 also introduces a VQA benchmark labeled VisWiz. The previous benchmark coverage is retained.

E2.justification: v4 newly includes LLaMA-2-7B as a language-only comparator in Table 10. Existing multimodal, segmentation, and tokenizer comparator sets remain intact; Table 14 reuses LLaVA-1.5 under a new training-data control, while Table 8 documents existing baselines.

E3.justification: v4 introduces substantive evaluation controls: varying text/multimodal training proportions before instruction tuning and retraining SeTokIM on the same dataset as LLaVA-1.5 for visual-understanding comparisons. Table 7 also revises the reported LLaVA-595K sample count from 665K to 595K. These additions and reported corrections do not establish that all retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds analyses of language retention versus training-data mixture and performance under matched training data. Table 11 extends the existing reconstruction-only ablation with a contrastive-only condition. The frozen-encoder and connector analyses are retained as Tables 12–13, and the segmentation examples are relocated rather than newly added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repeat counts, random seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The averages across MMLU subject categories in v4 are performance summaries, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v4 adds substantive language-retention, contrastive-only, and matched-data results in Tables 10, 11, and 14. It also revises reported VQAv2 from 78.7 to 78.5, MS-COCO FID from 8.3 to 8.5, MagicBrush L1 from 6.3 to 6.9, and ImageNet Top-1 from 76.4 to 75.4 in Tables 1–3. The matched-data results, including GQA 63.8 versus LLaVA-1.5's 62.0, concern a newly reported training condition, not a version-to-version performance gain.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 and Algorithm 1 retain the same mathematical definitions, objectives, and clustering operations. No theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: dynamically producing semantically complete visual tokens and integrating them into an MLLM for understanding, generation, editing, and segmentation. The added appendix evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v4 newly recommends a 7:3 language-to-vision mixture to limit language-performance degradation and interprets the matched-data comparison as support for better alignment. Appendix B expands the resolution limitation to discuss encoder fusion, low-resolution detail, and generalization; the model-scale and hallucination limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix D adds detokenizer implementation details, clarifies reconstruction/alignment dataset roles and overlapping training sources, and documents baseline backbones, encoders, resolutions, and data sizes in Table 8. Reported hardware changes from 16 to 64 H100 80GB GPUs, and the project-page address is updated. Most existing hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds the Eagle citation to the resolution discussion and a dedicated SEED-X reference, while removing references including OMG-LLaVA and SEEM; SEEM remains in the experimental comparison. Most other reference changes update publication metadata for existing works. The central novelty positioning is retained.

P1.justification: v4 makes localized prose edits, expands implementation and limitations explanations, adds Appendix D.4 on baselines, and moves the segmentation discussion into Appendix E. Publication headers, affiliations, contact information, and acknowledgments are updated, while the overall narrative and section organization remain largely stable.

P2.justification: v4 adds four tables: baseline configurations, language-mixture results, loss ablations, and the matched-data comparison. Existing illustrations are retained and rearranged: v3's segmentation Figure 5 becomes appendix Figure 8, with editing, token-mask, and reconstruction figures renumbered and reflowed. These are localized display changes rather than a visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The added language-retention and loss analyses, matched-data LLaVA comparison, and clearer training-data and baseline documentation improve evidential support and transparency. The gain is limited by reporting defects: v4 still has conflicting VQAv2 values of 78.5 in Table 1 and 78.7 in Tables 12–13, and the new loss-ablation Table 11 incorrectly carries an encoder-unfreezing caption. The method and central conclusions remain stable.
